overview: AutoSoup is a health-gated mushroom-stew chugger that fires the entire eat ceremony from one UpdateEvent. While health is at or below the Health threshold (default 15) and a stew sits in the hotbar, the module queues C09(soup slot), C08(use item), C07 DROP_ITEM and C09(restore) in a single tick, then resets its MSTimer for the Delay interval (default 150ms, range 0-500). The DROP_ITEM with BlockPos.ORIGIN and DOWN facing is the bowl drop that instant-soup servers expect after the heal; a RELEASE_USE_ITEM is never sent. When the hotbar is empty and stew remains in the inventory, the module shift-clicks it into the hotbar with the same simulated open-inventory ceremony AutoPot uses: C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT, a window-0 C0E click, and C0D close.

sections.p: The single onUpdate handler starts from a timer check: timer.hasTimePassed(delayValue) with delay defaulting to 150ms and reset() called after every successful action, so the cadence is a real 150ms-plus period rather than a one-shot latch. With health <= Health (default 15), InventoryUtils.findItem(36, 45, Items.mushroom_stew) locates the first stew in the hotbar container range. The tag property exposes the configured Health so the HUD shows the trigger value. Every packet is queued through mc.netHandler.addToSendQueue, so the four-packet ceremony lands in the order they are queued.

The hotbar path sends C09PacketHeldItemChange(soupInHotbar - 36), then C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the stew stack read from inventoryContainer.getSlot(soupInHotbar).stack (the single-argument form, BlockPos.ORIGIN plus face 255), then C07PacketPlayerDigging with action DROP_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN facing DOWN, then C09(currentItem) to restore the held slot. All four queue inside one event, so the server processes switch, use, drop and switch-back within a single tick. The DROP_ITEM is the bowl-drop idiom: on servers that complete consumption from the use packet, the empty bowl is pitched immediately. On a vanilla 32-tick use window the ceremony never completes the eat, so neither the heal nor the bowl materializes and the module is effectively silent there.

With the hotbar empty and stew present in the inventory (findItem(9, 36)) plus a free hotbar slot (InventoryUtils.hasSpaceHotbar), the module refills. OpenInv on requires an actually open GuiInventory and returns otherwise; SimulateInventory on performs the fabricated open: C16 OPEN_INVENTORY_ACHIEVEMENT, then mc.playerController.windowClick(0, soupInInventory, 0, 1), the C0E mode-1 shift-click, then C0D close. The client never renders a GUI, so the window exists only in the server ledger, and the timer resets after the refill as well. Whether the fork's windowClick syncs the held slot with a C09 is unverifiable here because the snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree.

files.label: AutoSoup.kt
files.explanation: The whole module: the health and timer gates, the four-packet same-tick ceremony (C09, C08, C07 DROP_ITEM, C09), and the C16-C0E-C0D simulated refill. The brief pins C08 and C09; the C07 and the refill C0E are part of the same cycle and belong in the prose. There is no release path: C07 is always DROP_ITEM, never RELEASE_USE_ITEM.

files.label: InventoryUtils.java (slot routing)
files.explanation: findItem walks the container slot range and returns the first stack whose item matches, and hasSpaceHotbar decides whether the refill path is allowed at all; both decide which ceremony the module runs on a given tick. The same helpers drive AutoPot's refill, so the eat/refill routing of the two modules shares one code path.

countering.label: ItemSwitchSpeed (same-tick eat restore)
countering.explanation: The direct hit: the C08 use arms usedSomething through InteractItemEvent, and the restore C09 in the same tick lands with a gap of 0 under minSwitchTicks 1, so every eat cycle punishes. Unlike the Rise eaters that delay the switch-back one tick and stay ahead of the default window, this module restores the slot in the same event, which is exactly the pattern the check was written for.

countering.label: InventoryActions (window-0 click with no window)
countering.explanation: The refill C0E is a ClickInventoryEvent while HawkPlayer.hasInventoryOpen() reads 0, because the C16 simulated open never sets Hawk's window ledger, so the check punishes and calls e.resync(), which undoes the local slot move. The hotbar eat path itself carries no C0E and evades this check; only the refill half of the cycle is exposed.

countering.label: FastClick (window-click ledger)
countering.explanation: The refill rate is one C0E per 150ms-plus cycle, far under the short-term buckets (ActionFrequency(5, 200L), limit 4) and the 15/s normal window, so the volume alone never trips it. The real weight is checkContainerInteraction scoring window-0 clicks that no container-open event precedes, plus the Improbable feed when fastClickImprobableWeight is configured; the eat ceremony itself is invisible to a click-ledger check.

countering.label: FastConsume (instant-soup ledger)
countering.explanation: Arc's InventoryListener stamps InventoryData.consumeTime on the edible right-click, and FastConsume compares it against the configured consume-time (default 1280ms) when the consume completes. On the instant-soup servers this module targets, the eat completes within a few milliseconds of the C08 and flags immediately; on a vanilla 32-tick server the one-tick ceremony never finishes the use, so the heal and the check both stay silent. The counter only bites exactly where the module works.
